proposals.title: Identify a numeric predicate with structural contrasts and counterexamples
proposals.trigger: Each oracle probe or final guess in a hidden numeric rule task
procedure: At the start and after new oracle feedback, call consult_capability_path with moduleId candidateProbe and input mode ordinal_predicate. Provide variable names, the complete observed query records with Boolean labels and obs-N sources, and three distinct valid probe levels. This is a numeric predicate task; do not use the code/feedback mode.

While candidateCount is above one, execute a legal split probe from the module rather than guessing or merely confirming all-equal positives. Append the actual feedback to records before consulting again. Only once candidates are separated may you form the final lambda; check the returned scope and validate against every oracle result.

Keep a table of queried tuples and observed Boolean results. Keep multiple consistent hypotheses; never remove a hypothesis merely because it is asymmetric in the input slots. Slot order is part of the problem.

Before concluding that only all-equal tuples are accepted, test every permutation of three distinct admissible magnitudes. There are six strict order patterns; two tested permutations do not cover the other four. Choose small valid values and generate all six permutations without duplicates.

For any accepted strict ordering, probe both adjacent equality boundaries and their reversals. Distinguish strict from non-strict comparisons, partial equality and all equality. Test the same structural pattern with negative and decimal values to distinguish order from sign, integrality and arithmetic identities.

When no order hypothesis fits, compare candidate arithmetic, sign and magnitude relations. Pick a tuple on which two surviving candidates predict opposite answers. Do not collect more examples from a cell on which they already agree.

Do not guess early just because ten probes agree with one candidate. A single-cell positive set does not prove necessity. If all-equal positives dominate, test the unvisited distinct-order cells before guessing. Use remaining probes to falsify the current rule.

Reserve the final available action for one lambda. Before submission evaluate the candidate against every recorded result; choose the simplest surviving relation supported by contrasts. Preserve the native Test Case and Final Guess syntax.
successSignals: Distinct order patterns and relevant equality boundaries are covered before a guess
The candidate survives discriminating tests outside its initial positive region
failureSignals: All positive observations have the same tie pattern
An untested permutation is silently treated as negative
Stopping because candidates were not enumerated rather than because they were separated
recovery: Return to the raw query table, list uncovered structural cells, and spend the next probe on an uncovered cell that separates plausible rules.
invariants: Never use a revealed answer from a prior attempt as a rule or a fixed final expression.
No fixed tuples or case-specific lambda are prescribed.
No final guess without checking every actual oracle result.
